description: Alterations to lower ground floor rear extension,  insertion of mezzanine bathroom, rooflights, and solar panels, and upgrading existing sash windows to double glazed timber sash windows.
decision_conditions: <div style="">A scheme for the provision and implementation of flood resilient and resistant construction details and measures for the site against surface water flood risk shall be submitted to and agreed, in writing with the LPA in consultation with the LLFA prior to the construction of the measures. The scheme shall be carried out in its entirety before the extension is occupied and; constructed and completed in accordance with the approved plans in line with current best practices.</div><div style=""><br></div><div style="">REASON:&nbsp;To ensure that the development will provide a sustainable drainage system. The condition is required to be discharged prior to the commencement of development to ensure that sustainable drainage is incorporated into the design of the development.</div>

<p>The roof of the rear extension hereby approved shall not be used as a terrace, balcony, or similar amenity area without the prior written consent of the local planning authority.</p><p>
REASON: In the interests of neighbouring amenities.</p>

<p>Full details of materials, including a sample of bricks to be used on the external surfaces of the building, shall be submitted to and approved by the local planning authority, in writing, before any work commences on site. The development shall not be carried out otherwise than in accordance with the details thus approved.<br style=""><br style="">REASON: To ensure that special regard is paid to protecting the special architectural and historic interest and integrity of the building.&nbsp;</p>

<div style="">Prior to commencement of works, full details and specifications of the green roofs shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the local planning authority. The submission shall include the following:<br><ul style=""><li style="margin-left: 15px;">Detailed drawings of a roof plan identifying where the green roofs will be located and the measurement of their coverage; this should include other structures on the roof, including the location of PV panels, roof lights, and access points where applicable, and their relationship with the green roof;</li><li style="margin-left: 15px;">The design of the green roof should be in line with GRO’s code of best practice;</li><li style="margin-left: 15px;">Section drawings demonstrating a minimum substrate depth of no less than 80mm for a sedum roof;</li><li style="margin-left: 15px;">Details of the drainage system for the roof;</li><li style="margin-left: 15px;">Details of the planting mix, including a minimum of 9+ species for the sedum roof;</li><li style="margin-left: 15px;">All roofs to be sown with a wide mix of species.</li><li style="margin-left: 15px;">Management and maintenance plan, including access arrangements, irrigation, and general maintenance actions.</li></ul>Within a month of the first occupation of the development, evidence must be submitted to and approved by the local planning authority that the green roof has been delivered in line with the approved details, unless otherwise agreed in writing. The green roof shall be retained thereafter for the lifetime of the development in accordance with the approved management and maintenance plan.<br></div><div style=""><br></div><div style="">Reason: To promote biodiversity on site.</div>
